label: Formulated the Coloniality of Power matrix
description: Quijano articulated how the invention of 'race' as an instrument of domination during the conquest of the Americas constituted the foundational matrix of modern global capitalism and Eurocentric knowledge.
historicalContext: Published in 2000 in Nepantla: Views from South, emerging from decades of sociological field research in Peru and across Latin America.
dialecticalTension: Distinguishes historical colonialism (which can formally end via administrative independence) from coloniality (the pervasive civilizational power matrix that endures).

citations.author: Aníbal Quijano
citations.work: Coloniality of Power, Eurocentrism, and Latin America
citations.quote: The racial axis has a colonial origin and character, but it has proven to be more durable and stable than the colonialism in whose matrix it was established.

citations.author: Walter D. Mignolo
citations.work: The Darker Side of Western Modernity: Global Futures, Decolonial Options

label: Re-theorized global capitalism through racial division of labor
description: Quijano expanded Marx's analysis of primitive accumulation and capital, showing that world capital has always integrated heterogeneous forms of unfree labor articulated along racialized lines.
historicalContext: Developed in critical dialogue with Latin American orthodox Marxism and dependency theorists throughout the 1980s and 1990s.
dialecticalTension: Critiques orthodox Marxist class reductionism by proving that race and coloniality are constitutive, not merely superstructural, to the capitalist world-system.

citations.author: Aníbal Quijano
citations.quote: Capitalism became from its origin a world system articulating all forms of labor control around capital, organized along racial hierarchies.

label: Elevated the color line to the foundational axis of global modernity
description: Quijano resonated with Du Bois's prophetic insight that 'the problem of the twentieth century is the problem of the color line', formalizing it into a worldwide sociological matrix of power.
historicalContext: Comparative sociological synthesis of Pan-African and Latin American critical theories of race and empire.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes Du Bois's double consciousness and racial capitalism with Latin American historical dependency and coloniality.

citations.author: W.E.B. Du Bois
citations.quote: The problem of the twentieth century is the problem of the color-line,—the relation of the darker to the lighter races of men in Asia and Africa, in America and the islands of the sea.

citations.author: Ramón Grosfoguel
citations.work: The Epistemic Decolonial Turn: Beyond Political-Economy Paradigms

label: Collaborated on the Modernity/Coloniality Decolonial Research Program
description: Dussel and Quijano forged the collaborative intellectual core of the Latin American Decolonial collective, weaving the philosophy of liberation with the sociological critique of the coloniality of power.
historicalContext: Formed through the Modernity/Coloniality/Decoloniality (MCD) working group meetings across Binghamton, Caracas, and Mexico City in the late 1990s and 2000s.
dialecticalTension: Harmonizes philosophical ethics of exteriority with structural sociological mapping of global capitalist racialization.

citations.author: Enrique Dussel
citations.quote: Quijano has demonstrated that the coloniality of power is the other face of modernity; there is no modernity without coloniality.

citations.author: Arturo Escobar
citations.work: Worlds and Knowledges Otherwise: The Latin American Modernity/Coloniality Research Program
